name: Brundarok
text: Bronze rail. Carts ride it up to 0.6 blocks per tick, half again vanilla speed. Curves, slopes and junctions work like a normal rail. Age III.

name: Brundavoss
text: Bronze powered rail. Boosts a cart when powered, stops it when not. Caps at 0.6 blocks per tick. Age III.

name: Sorvanquil
text: Steel rail. Carts ride it up to 0.9 blocks per tick, more than twice vanilla speed. Age V.

name: Sorvaleth
text: Steel powered rail. A stronger boost than bronze, same stop when unpowered. Caps at 0.9 blocks per tick. Age V.

name: Zephrakund
text: High-speed rail. Carts ride it up to 1.2 blocks per tick, three times vanilla speed. Keep curves gentle. Age VI.

name: Zephravoss
text: High-speed powered rail. The strongest boost, caps at 1.2 blocks per tick. Age VI.

name: Haldurmek
text: Station rail. Stops a cart that rolls onto it and holds it until the rail is powered, or until its timer ends. Use it bare-handed to cycle the timer: signal only, 2, 5, 15 or 60 seconds. A coupled follower follows its leader instead. Age V.

name: Quelvarith
text: Coupling chain. Use it on one cart, then on a second: the first leads, the second follows at a fixed spacing and is pulled along, so a row of carts runs as a train. A link breaks if the carts get more than 8 blocks apart. Age V.

name: Snithrekel
text: Chain cutters. Sneak and use on a cart to cut its link and get the chain back. Age V.

name: Block Signal
text: Faces a rail and guards the stretch of connected track from there, up to 32 rails each way, round curves and slopes. Red and a redstone signal of 15 while any minecart is on that stretch, green and 0 otherwise. Wire it to a station rail or a powered rail upstream to keep trains apart. Age V.

name: One-Way Rail
text: A rail that lets carts through one way only. The arrow on it points north or east; use it bare-handed to turn it round. A cart that rolls on against the arrow is turned back. Place it on a straight stretch. Age V.

name: Destination Rail
text: Routes carts by name. It gives a redstone signal of 15 while a cart whose name matches its channel stands on it. Use it bare-handed to cycle the channel: any cart, or the letters A to P, matched against the cart name (name a cart "C" with a name tag). Power a three-way junction rail with it and the named carts take the branch. Age V.

name: Cart Loader
text: Stands over a rail with a chest, barrel or tank on top. Every 8 ticks it moves up to 8 items, or 250 mB of fluid, between the container and the cart standing under it: loading from the container, or unloading into it (use it bare-handed to flip). Works on any cart that offers an item or fluid handler, including chest carts, hopper carts and the tank wagons from the yards. Redstone switches it off. Age V.

name: Locking Rail
text: Stops a cart that rolls onto it and keeps it there. Use it bare-handed to change mode. Latch (amber) holds the cart until the rail goes from unpowered to powered, a redstone pulse; a rail already powered when the cart arrived does not release it. Interlock (green) holds the cart until the 32 rails ahead are clear of other carts, then lets it go. Age V.

name: Chest (freight)
text: Chest for freight. Holds 27 stacks. Break it and the items stay inside the item you get. Age I.

name: Pallet
text: Pallet load. Holds 18 stacks and carries up to 1.5 t. Stacks two or three high inside a container. Age II.

name: Barrel
text: Barrel. Holds 18 stacks and carries up to 300 kg. Age II.

name: Crate
text: Crate. Holds 54 stacks and carries up to 1.2 t. Age II.

name: Shipping container, 20 ft
text: Shipping container, 20 ft. A walkable box with a 2 by 2 by 5 block interior, rated 28 t. Set it down with the item; swing the door at the far end by using it; lift it back into one item, cargo and all, with a cargo hook or a crane. Age VI.

name: Shipping container, 40 ft
text: Shipping container, 40 ft. Interior 2 by 2 by 11 blocks, rated 26.7 t. Age VI.

name: Reefer container, 20 ft
text: Reefer container, 20 ft. A container with a refrigeration unit at the closed end, drawing 4 kW. Interior 2 by 2 by 4. Age VI.

name: Reefer container, 40 ft
text: Reefer container, 40 ft. Interior 2 by 2 by 10, refrigeration unit at the closed end, 4 kW. Age VI.

name: Tank container, 20 ft
text: Tank container, 20 ft. Holds 26,000 litres of fluid in an ISO frame. Pump it empty before lifting. Age VI.

name: Cargo hook
text: Cargo hook. Use it on a container wall or door to lift the whole box into one item, up to 35 t. Age VI.

name: Loading dock
text: Loading dock. Faces a container up to three blocks ahead and offers its cargo to storage network cables, hoppers, pipes and depot workers. The comparator reads how full the container is. Age V.

name: Rift dock
text: Rift dock. Serves the container at its partner, the other rift dock on the same channel in any dimension. Bare hand cycles the channel. Age VIII.

name: Timetable
text: Use on station rails in order to write the stops of a run, then use on a cart to give it the schedule; it loops. A scheduled cart stops only at its next stop and runs only with a rider aboard (a player, villager or other crew), unless it is autonomous: a capable vehicle type with an Autonomy Module fitted. Sneak and use in the air to wipe it. Age V.

name: Autonomy Module
text: Use on a vehicle whose type is capable of autonomy (the entity type tag diaithircarts:autonomy_capable) to fit it. A scheduled vehicle with a module runs with no crew, and its crew jobs can be retired. Without one it needs a rider aboard. Age VII.

name: Cart Reader
text: Put it under a rail. Gives a redstone signal for the cart above it: 0 none, 1 a cart with no schedule, 2 to 13 a scheduled cart heading for that stop (signal minus 2; 13 means stop 11 or any later stop), 14 a scheduled cart with no crew waiting for one, 15 an autonomous cart. Age V.

name: Narrow-Gauge Rail
text: Narrow-gauge rail (3 ft). Cheap and light: it takes tight curves and steep grades, so it suits mountains and mines, but carts cap at 0.5 blocks per tick and narrow vehicles carry about 40% of the payload and are limited in weight. Does not connect with standard gauge. Age III.

name: Narrow-Gauge Powered Rail
text: Narrow-gauge powered rail. Boosts a narrow-gauge vehicle when powered, stops it when not. Caps at 0.5 blocks per tick. Age III.

name: Dual-Gauge Rail
text: Three rails laid so both gauges run on one track. Narrow and standard vehicles both pass, at the narrow cap of 0.5 blocks per tick and with the standard gauge's wide curves. Use it at yards and transfer stations. Age V.

name: Dual-Gauge Powered Rail
text: Dual-gauge powered rail. Boosts vehicles of either gauge when powered. Age V.
